web_evidence.title: Cross My Heart — Penguin Books sample
web_evidence.note: Authorized publisher sample spans the prologue and multiple early chapters, alternating Alex Cross’s participating first-person narration with sustained third-person chapters following Marcus Sunday and other characters.

web_evidence.title: Cross My Heart by James Patterson — Excerpt
web_evidence.note: Copyrighted sustained excerpt shows a first-person Alex prologue, third-person Marcus Sunday in Chapter 1, first-person Alex in Chapter 2, and continued switches between the two persons through later excerpted chapters.

web_evidence.title: A Profile of Detective Alex Cross, Forensic Psychologist

person_note: The book sustains two base-narration modes: Alex Cross narrates his own chapters in first person, while Marcus Sunday and other non-Alex scenes are narrated in third person. The first-person passages are therefore not embedded documents or isolated thoughts, and the third-person passages are full antagonist chapters rather than brief external references inside Alex’s narration. The input quotes independently expose both modes, and the authorized opening excerpts reproduce the same chapter-level switching. The main limitation is that the strongest prose sources cover the opening rather than every chapter, but the interior quote evidence and explicit series-level description corroborate the continuing structure, with no credible contrary evidence.
